newsitem.title: USA: Nine West says SEC probe focuses on U.S. Shoe business.
newsitem.headline: Nine West says SEC probe focuses on U.S. Shoe business.

text.p: Nine West Group said Wednesday a Securities and Exchange Commission probe of its revenue-booking policies is focused on businesses it acquired from U.S. Shoe Corp. and involves its wholesaling business.
The Stamford, Conn.-based women's shoe manufacturer and retailer said it learned on May 1 that the probe had become a formal investigation as of April 10.

Nine West's stock rose $2.125 to $34.625 on the New York Stock Exchange at mid-afternoon as investors were relieved to learn the focus of the probe appears to be accounting policies that were in place when Nine West acquired U.S. Shoe.

On Tuesday, the company's shares slid about 18 percent when it filed an amended annual report with the SEC that disclosed the investigation. Nine West's brands include Enzo Angiolini, Easy Spirit, Bandolino and Evan Picone.
"We have no idea at this point in time when it will be completed," said Robert Galvin, Nine West's chief financial officer, during a conference call.
Galvin said "as far as we're aware," the SEC probe deals with accounting practices during 1995 and is not expected to have "a material adverse effect" on the company.

Nine West is cooperating with the SEC, he said. The probe has not reached the stage of negotiations, and the company is not aware of what triggered the SEC's decision to make the investigation a formal one.
Nine West said it does not expect to restate earnings.
The company bought the footwear division of Cincinnati-based U.S. Shoe in May 1995. This gave it five domestic footwear manufacturing facilities but it has closed two of them since April.
Nine West had said in its annual report that it planned to close three of the factories and reconfigure or close the other two to cut costs and beef up global sourcing.
